title: Why our ancestors started walking upright
summary: There are at least twelve distinct hypotheses for how and why human bipedalism evolved. It is dated to at least 4 million years ago, possibly 7 million with Sahelanthropus.
why: Upright walking is one of the earliest traits that set our lineage apart.
question: Why did human ancestors evolve to walk on two legs?
evidence: Bipedalism clear by about 4 million years ago (Australopithecus afarensis); possibly 7 million (Sahelanthropus); Danuvius suggests about 12 million.
wouldSettle: Well-dated early hominin skeletons with environmental data showing what habitat and behaviour accompanied first upright walking.

theories.name: Postural feeding
theories.idea: Ancestors stood upright mainly to reach food in trees.

theories.name: Savanna and travel efficiency
theories.idea: Walking upright was cheaper for moving between scattered trees in open country.

theories.name: Provisioning (Lovejoy)
theories.idea: Males carrying food to mates and offspring favoured upright walking.

theories.name: Thermoregulation
theories.idea: Standing upright reduced sun exposure and helped the body stay cool.
